questions.text:
Consider the following two statements.

S1: If a candidate is known to be corrupt, then he will not be elected
S2: If a candidate is kind, he will be elected

Which one of the following statements follows from S1 and S2 as per sound inference rules of logic?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- S1: corrupt [latex]\rightarrow\neg[/latex] elected, whose contrapositive is elected [latex]\rightarrow\neg[/latex] corrupt
- S2: kind [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] elected

Chaining: kind [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] elected [latex]\rightarrow\neg[/latex] corrupt.

Answer: If a person is kind, he is not known to be corrupt

questions.text: The cardinality of the power set of { 0, 1, 2,..., 10 } is _________.
questions.solution:
The set {0, 1, ..., 10} has 11 elements.

[latex]|P(S)|=2^{11}=2048[/latex]

Answer: 2048

questions.text: Let R be the relation on the set of positive integers such that aRb if and only if a and b are distinct and have a common divisor other than 1. Which one of the following statements about R is true?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Not reflexive: a and b must be distinct.
- Symmetric: a common divisor of a, b is also a common divisor of b, a.
- Not transitive: 2 R 6 and 6 R 3, but 2 and 3 have no common divisor other than 1.

Answer: R is symmetric but not reflexive and not transitive

R is transitive but not reflexive and not symmetric
R is symmetric but not reflexive and not transitive

questions.text: The number of divisors of 2100 is _____ .
questions.solution:
[latex]2100=2^2\times3\times5^2\times7[/latex]

Number of divisors = (2 + 1)(1 + 1)(2 + 1)(1 + 1) = 36

Answer: 36
